title: Microsoft Purview: permanently delete OneDrive and SharePoint files with Priority cleanup (Worldwide)
summary: Hold: the briefing treats recovery after permanent deletion as an unanswered question, but Microsoft documents an exceptional support-ticket recovery process, subject to approval and without any guarantee. The rollout dates, licensing, default state and control calls are supported; the policy-creation path also needs a small clarification.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a permanent-deletion option for Priority cleanup policies targeting OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.quote: Ability to select hard delete configuration for a Priority cleanup policy for OneDrive and SharePoint content and skip recycle bins.

claims.claim: The roadmap description says retention policies and labels keep deleted OneDrive and SharePoint content in recycle bins for 93 days.
claims.quote: M365 retention labels policies and M365 retention policies do not hard delete content immediately and keeps the data in Recycle Bins for 93 days for ODSP.

claims.claim: The notice positions permanent deletion as reducing exposure from Copilot-related content such as Teams transcripts.
claims.quote: Review your organization’s data risk and retention strategy, especially for Copilot-generated content such as Teams transcripts.

claims.claim: The roadmap description identifies data spillage as a use case.
claims.quote: Priority Cleanup feature allows users to bypass retention, and eDiscovery holds ... or manage data spillage scenarios.

claims.claim: Permanent deletion is admin-opt-in and is not enabled by default.
claims.quote: This capability is not enabled by default and requires explicit admin configuration.

claims.claim: User workflows do not change unless an admin configures and applies a priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: The tenant-level Priority cleanup control is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.claim: Review-set data is automatically deleted when an eDiscovery admin deletes the entire case.
claims.quote: This data is automatically deleted when the entire eDiscovery case is deleted by an eDiscovery admin.

claims.claim: Learn's overview says Priority cleanup can override Preservation Lock for delete-only settings.
claims.quote: Because the deletion from priority cleanup can override existing holds and even Preservation Lock when the retention settings are for delete-only

claims.claim: The same Learn page's Limitations section excludes Preservation Lock delete-only items outside simulation mode.
claims.quote: In simulation mode, items under preservation lock where the retention settings are configured for delete-only may show up. These items are not actually in scope for priority cleanup outside simulation mode.

claims.claim: Learn describes multiple approvals, specific roles and auditing as safeguards.
claims.quote: the process requires multiple approvals, specific roles, and is audited.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is automatically added to Organization Management, allowing its existing members access without a new assignment.
claims.quote: This role is automatically added to the Organization Management role group but must be manually added to any other role group.

claims.claim: The last person to edit the policy cannot also turn it on.
claims.quote: The last person to edit the policy can't also turn it on.

claims.claim: Each item requires at least one other person to approve deletion in addition to the policy creator.
claims.quote: each item subject to priority cleanup always requires at least one other person to approve the deletion in addition to the person who created the priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: Items subject to eDiscovery holds require eDiscovery admin approval.
claims.quote: If an item is also subject to one or more eDiscovery holds, eDiscovery admin approval is also required.

claims.claim: Learn recommends leaving a continuous policy running for stale Teams recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: Because these files are continually created, leave the priority cleanup policy running to automatically find and delete the stale files.

claims.claim: Whether Microsoft documents any recovery route after Priority cleanup permanent deletion remains an open question.
claims.quote: In an exceptional scenario, customers can submit a support ticket to request recovery. Recovery is subject to Microsoft review and approval and is attempted only on a best-effort basis. Recovery isn't guaranteed.
claims.fix: Remove the final Open questions bullet: the cited Learn page already answers it. If retaining a replacement statement, use: 'Microsoft documents an exceptional support-ticket recovery request, subject to Microsoft review and approval, attempted only on a best-effort basis and not guaranteed; there is no customer-accessible recovery option.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/priority-cleanup-permanent-deletion#understand-permanent-deletion-and-recovery-limitations.

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant Priority cleanup switch also applies to Exchange, as well as SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for Exchange as well as for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.quote: Update internal governance or compliance documentation to reflect this new deletion capability.

claims.claim: A permanent deletion cannot be undone from the recycle bin.
claims.quote: Deleted content bypasses the recycle bins and isn't recoverable under ordinary circumstances.
